sentences.text:
THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF M.V. ACT,
1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 02-05-2012, PASSED IN MVC.NO.170/2008 ON THE FILE OF THE DISTRICT JUDGE AND MEMBER, MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIM TRIBUNAL, GADAG, AWARDING THE COMPENSATION OF RS.10,000/-
WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 6% P.A., FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ITS REALISATION.
THIS MFA COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Respondent No.2 - insurer in MVC No.170 of 2008 on the file of the learned District Judge and MACT, Gadag (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity)

, is impugning the judgment and award dated 02.05.2012, awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- with interest at 6% per annum,
from the date of petition till its realisation holding that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
2. Parties are referred to as per their rank and status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are that, the claimant filed the claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation for the injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.

It is contended that on 22.01.2008 at about 5.30 p.m. the claimant NC: 2023:KHC-D:7493 was traveling in the Ambulance - the Maruthi Van bearing registration No.KA-26/3047 owned by respondent No.1 and insured with respondent No.2.
Due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver, the ambulance turtled to the left side of the road.
As a result of which, the claimant sustained injures.
She was shifted to District Hospital, Gadag where she took treatment as inpatient.

She has spent huge amount for her treatment and therefore, claimed compensation from respondent Nos.1 and 2.
4.
Respondent No.1 has filed the objections denying the contention taken by the claimant.

However,
contended that the vehicle in question was insured with respondent No.2.
Therefore, it is respondent No.2 who is liable to pay compensation.
5. Respondent No.2 - insurer has also filed objection denying the contention taken by the claimant.
It is also contended that respondent No.1 knowingly permitted the person who was not having valid driving licence to drive the same and thereby, violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text:
On the basis of these pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:
"1. Whether the petitioner proves that petitioner sustained injuries on 22.01.2008 at 5.30 p.m. near Harlapur cross on Gadag-Koppal road, when the Maruti Ambulance Van, in which petitioner was traveling with her brother's wife, turtled down by the left side of road, due to rash and negligent driving of said Maruti Ambulance Van by it's driver?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to the compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order?"
7. The claimant examined herself as PW1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P6 in support of her contention.
Respondents examined as RW1 and got marked Exs.R1 to R5 in support of their defence.

The Tribunal after taking into consideration all these materials on record, answered issue No.1 in the Affirmative and issued No.2 partly in the Affirmative and came to the conclusion that the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Being aggrieved by the same, the insurer is before this Court.
9. Heard Smt Preeti Shashank, learned counsel for the appellant.
Respondents served, but they remained absent and unrepresented.
10. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the offending vehicle was used as ambulance i.e., transport vehicle.
The driver of the same was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
As per Ex.R1, driver was holding LMV(NT) licence and therefore, there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

She has also referred to Ex.R2 letter issued by Regional Transport Officer,
Gadag clarifying that the vehicle involved in the accident is a transport vehicle and the driver was holding licence to drive LMV (NT) only.
Therefore, it is a clear case of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
But the Tribunal has not taken into consideration this aspect of the matter.
Hence, it calls for interference.
Accordingly, she prays for allowing the appeal.

In view of the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal suffers from any infirmity and calls for interference by this Court?"

sentences.text:
My answer to the above point is in the 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 12.
The only point raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is with regard to the validity of the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is admitted that the vehicle involved in the accident is a transport vehicle and the driver was having LMV (NT) licence.

Ex.R1 is the endorsement issued by the Regional Transport Officer, Gadag, according to which, the driver of the offending vehicle was authorized to drive LMV (NT) w.e.f. 28.12.2007 which was valid upto 27.12.2027.
The accident had occurred on 22.01.2008 i.e., during the validity of the said driving licence.

Ex.R2 makes the position clear that the driver was holding licence to drive LMV(NT), and the ambulance is classified as transport vehicle NC: 2023:KHC-D:7493 and the driver is not authorized to drive the transport vehicle.
Therefore, it is contended that the driver was not holding valid and effective driving licence.

13. It is relevant to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Mukund Dewangan Vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 1, wherein, the Full bench of Hon'ble Apex Court considered the question referred for the decision by Larger Bench and answered the same as under:
(i) 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.
(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle 2017 ACJ 2011 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7493 or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

(iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle"
in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h)
with expression 'transport vehicle' as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.

It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sharavva W/O Pundapp Bhavikatti on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9069642/
4 purview of section 10(2)(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Sharavva W/O Pundapp Bhavikatti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor NC:
2023:KHC-D:7493 vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.
(Emphasis supplied)

Thus, the position of law is very well settled that the transport vehicle are not excluded from the definition of LMV by virtue of Amendment Act 54 of 1994 and no separate endorsement on the license is required to drive the transport vehicle, which is classified as LMV.
14.
Under such circumstances, I do not find any merit in the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant.
Hence, the appeal should fail.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is dismissed with costs.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 02.05.2012 passed in MVC No.170 of 2008 on the file of the District Judge and MACT, Gadag, is hereby confirmed.

Registry is directed to send back the Trial Court records along with copy of this judgment.
